children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Wednesday.
WHEAT - Down 6 to 8 cents per bushel
CBOT wheat
reached the highest level since February 2023 and then pulled back.
The market has rallied as escalating attacks have interrupted Russian and Ukrainian grain exports from the Black Sea region.
Ukraine's grain exports declined by about 58% in August, compared to a year earlier, its agriculture ministry said.
Turkey's president said a mechanism was needed to permanently ensure the safety of commercial maritime transport in the Black Sea.
Russia's foreign minister said he saw no grounds to resume a deal that allowed the safe export of Ukrainian grain via the Black Sea.
, the world's biggest wheat exporter, said separately that it was suspending export duties on grain until the end of 2026.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last down 6-3/4 cents at $7.75-3/4 per bushel. The market set contract highs before retreating.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last down 11 cents at $8.34-1/4 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last 5-1/4 cents lower at $7.71-1/2 a bushel.
CORN - Down 7 to 9 cents
CBOT corn
backpedaled after reaching a July 2023 high.
Profit-taking dragged down grain prices after markets have rallied and as traders awaited estimates on U.S. corn and soybean crops.
Commodity firm Allendale projected U.S. corn production at 15.833 billion bushels and soybean production at 4.515 billion bushels.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 8-1/4 cents at $5.37-3/4 per bushel. The market earlier set contract highs.
SOYBEANS - Down 13 to 15 cents
CBOT soybeans
set the highest price since December 2023 before falling on profit-taking.
U.S. export demand and uncertainty over yield potential recently supported prices.
Exporters sold 202,000 metric tons of U.S. soybeans to
, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last down 14-1/2 cents at $13.03-1/4 per bushel. Earlier, the market set contract highs in deferred futures.
